title: Mission Update & Completion
description: -11 gave the mission its own URL. Both of the agent's post-approval operations happen at POST {mission_endpoint}/{mission_s256}, discriminated by an `action` member: `update` records a change in the work, and `completion` proposes that the mission is finished. Completion used to live on the interaction endpoint; it moved because it is a lifecycle transition, not transport — creation and completion have the same shape, the agent proposes and the person decides.

approved_tools.name: ReportWriter

steps.label: POST /mission/{s256} {action: update} → 200 + update digest

request_body.description:
# Scope of the feedback set changed

The April export was incomplete; 1,247 records are available rather than the ~900 assumed at approval. Continuing with the larger set — same tools, same report.

annotations: action is REQUIRED at a mission's own URL. A PS MUST reject a missing or unrecognized action with 400 — the same discriminator the pending route uses.

An update does not change the mission. The blob is immutable, mission_s256 is unchanged, and every token carrying it stays valid — which is the point: the agent keeps working while the record catches up.
What it changes is the context the PS evaluates against. From acceptance onward the mission's meaning is the blob plus its accepted updates, and an audit MUST read both.
The PS returns the update's own s256 — the digest of the bytes it persisted — so the sequence of accepted updates is verifiable, not merely stored.
The PS MAY instead return 202 while the person reviews the update. Both narrowing and broadening can warrant that.

steps.label: POST /mission/{s256} {action: completion, summary} → 202

request_body.summary:
# Q2 Feedback Analysis Complete

Read 1,247 feedback records across April–June and produced `q2-feedback-summary.pdf` on the shared drive.

**Headline numbers:** avg rating 4.2 ⭐ · 68% positive · 22% neutral · 10% negative.

**Top three themes:** (1) onboarding flow friction, (2) billing page clarity, (3) requests for dark mode.

annotations: Completion moved off the interaction endpoint in -11. It is a lifecycle transition, not something the agent needs the person for as transport.
The mission is named by the path, not by a body member: POST {mission_endpoint}/{mission_s256}.
action=completion and summary (Markdown) are both REQUIRED.
The interaction endpoint keeps interaction, payment and question — the things the agent genuinely cannot do itself.
The PS returns 202 because the person has to decide. The agent proposes completion; it does not declare it.

annotations: PS notifies the user (push notification, email, or in-app) that the agent proposes completion.
User reviews the Markdown summary at the PS's UI.
User clicks Accept — PS will terminate the mission and return 200 to the agent.
Alternatively, the user MAY respond with follow-up questions via clarification (§1179), keeping the mission active.

steps.label: Poll /pending/c5d9a3b7 → 200 (mission terminated)
annotations: The person accepted — the PS terminates the mission and the next poll returns 200.
A mission has two states: active and terminated. A terminated mission MUST NOT return to active.

The PS records why, alongside the mission rather than inside the immutable blob: completed, revoked, expired, superseded or administrative. The set is open, and a reader that does not recognize a reason keeps the terminated state and treats it as an opaque audit value.
Later requests naming this mission_s256 return mission_terminated, with termination_reason as an OPTIONAL member for context — expired invites proposing a new mission, revoked does not.
Existing auth tokens carrying this mission_s256 stay valid until they expire. The PS will not issue new ones.
Alternatively the person responds with follow-up questions via clarification chat and the mission stays active. That is the most common path.
